Under rule-only prompting, the best of the 11 evaluated video backends produces the required endings for both cases in 32% of pairs. For MiniMax-H3, specifying the required endings raises this rate from 32% to 64%, while the full harness reaches 92% with the same frozen model. These results support separating rule execution from video rendering for world interactions with hidden state.
papers.title_ko: 상태 세계 모델: 규칙을 실행하고 픽셀을 생성하다
papers.background: 기존 세계 모델은 단일 이미지에서 동작 조건부 영상을 생성할 수 있고, 많은 연구가 카메라 이동을 중심으로 사용자가 생성된 장면을 탐색할 수 있게 한다. 그러나 탐색만으로는 현재 프레임에 보이지 않는 상태가 결과에 영향을 줄 때, 동작이 지속되는 규칙을 따르는 것을 보장하지 못한다.
papers.summary: 본 연구는 세계 진화와 영상 렌더링을 분리하는 Stateful Harness를 제안하며, 지정된 규칙에 따라 진화하는 세계 상태를 유지하고 동결된 비디오 모델로 각 이벤트를 렌더링한 뒤 생성된 클립으로 다음 턴의 세계 상태를 갱신한다. 각 턴에서 사용자의 동작을 해석해 이벤트 지시문으로 컴파일하고, 편집 가능한 3D 씬의 미리보기 클립이 공간 및 카메라 안내를 제공한다. 규칙 준수도를 평가하기 위해 초기 프레임과 동작은 같지만 숨겨진 상태와 필요한 결과가 다른 50쌍의 반사실 쌍으로 구성된 WorldState-Bench를 구축했다. 규칙만 프롬프팅할 때 11개 비디오 백엔드 중 최선은 32%의 쌍에서 두 경우 모두 필요한 끝장을 생성했으며, MiniMax-H3에서 필요한 끝장을 명시하면 64%로, 동일한 동결 모델을 사용한 전체 하네스는 92%를 달성했다.
papers.limitations: (추정) 편집 가능한 3D 씬 미리보기와 명시된 규칙에 의존하므로, 3D 표현이 어렵거나 규칙이 불완전한 개방형 환경에서는 적용 범위가 제한될 수 있다. (추정) WorldState-Bench가 50쌍의 반사실 쌍으로 구성되어 있어 다양한 규칙과 장기 상호작용에 대한 일반화 성능은 추가 검증이 필요하다. (추정) 동결된 비디오 모델의 생성 품질과 상태 업데이트 정확도에 따라 최종 규칙 준수율이 달라질 수 있어, 모델 변경에 따른 안정성은 초록만으로는 확인하기 어렵다.

papers.title: ACEdit: Stable Multi-Turn Image Editing via Asymmetric Conditioning
papers.abstract: Image editing models produce impressive results for individual edits, but their quality often deteriorates over multiple editing turns. Each editing turn introduces small distribution shifts that accumulate over successive edits, creating a gap between the input distributions encountered during the editor's original training and multi-turn inference. We introduce a training scheme that makes multi-turn image editing stable under this accumulating distribution shift. A key is to force the editor to operate on its own outputs from previous editing turns during training, bringing the principle of Self-Forcing to image editing. The main challenge is that self-generated editing trajectories deviate from ground-truth trajectories, making direct supervision unreliable. We address this challenge through a distillation objective that leverages a teacher image editor to provide a reliable training signal when the model operates on its own previous outputs. We introduce an asymmetric conditioning scheme: while the student performs edits sequentially on its own outputs, the teacher remains anchored to the original clean image and receives a compound editing instruction. Experiments show substantially reduced degradation over long multi-turn sequences while maintaining editing quality and instruction adherence.
papers.title_ko: ACEdit: 비대칭 조건화를 통한 안정적인 다중 턴 이미지 편집
papers.background: 이미지 편집 모델은 단일 편집에서는 뛰어난 결과를 내지만, 여러 턴에 걸쳐 편집할수록 품질이 저하되는 문제가 있다. 각 편집 턴은 작은 분포 시프트(distribution shift)를 유발하고, 이는 누적되어 원래 학습 시 입력 분포와 다중 턴 추론 시 입력 분포 사이의 격차를 만든다.
papers.summary: 이 논문은 다중 턴 이미지 편집(multi-turn image editing)에서 누적 분포 시프트에 대해 안정성을 확보하기 위한 학습 방식을 제안한다. 학습 시 편집기가 이전 턴의 자기 생성 출력 위에서 동작하도록 하여 Self-Forcing 원리를 적용하고, 자기 생성 궤적이 ground-truth에서 벗어나 직접 감독이 신뢰할 수 없는 문제를 교사 모델 기반 증류(distillation) 목적 함수로 해결한다. 비대칭 조건화(asymmetric conditioning) 방식에서는 학생이 자기 출력 위에서 순차 편집을 수행하는 반면, 교사는 원래 깨끗한 이미지에 고정되어 복합 편집 지시를 받는다. 실험 결과, 긴 다중 턴 시퀀스에서 품질 저하가 크게 줄고 편집 품질과 지시 준수도가 유지됨을 보였다.
papers.limitations: (추정) 자기 생성 편집 궤적에 의존하는 학습 방식은 실제 사용자 편집 의도가 누적되는 복잡한 다중 턴 시나리오까지 완전히 보장하지 못할 수 있다. (추정) 교사 모델에 대한 증류 의존도가 높아 교사 편집기의 품질이나 지시 표현 범위에 따라 성능이 제한될 수 있다. (추정) 긴 다중 턴 안정성만 강조되어 정량 지표, 계산 비용, 다양한 편집 작업에 대한 일반화 성능은 판단하기 어렵다.

papers.title: Harnessing Textual Refusal Directions for Multimodal Safety
papers.abstract: Safety in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) depends on unsafe multimodal data for post-training alignment or activation steering. However, such data is hard to collect, must be gathered anew for each modality, and its collection and distribution raise ethical and legal concerns. In this work, we relax this constraint and investigate whether textual refusal directions, extracted directly from the LLM backbone, generalize across modalities (i.e., image, video). Preliminary findings confirm this ability, though effectiveness is conditioned by layer selection, steering strength, and cross-modal alignment, with the latter causing safe multimodal inputs to be spuriously steered toward refusal. Building on this, we introduce Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering (MARS), a lightweight training-free approach that injects multimodal safety without the need for multimodal safety data. MARS corrects modality misalignment via activation centering, adaptively scales steering strength within a geometrically defined trust region, and selects the optimal intervention layer, operating at the first generated token. Evaluated on five SOTA MLLMs across safety, utility, and video jailbreak, MARS achieves consistent safety gains while preserving utility up to over-refusal. MARS reveals that safety-relevant structure is shared across modalities and that textual refusal directions are a powerful and underexplored foundation for multimodal alignment.
papers.title_ko: 멀티모달 안전을 위한 텍스트 거부 방향 활용
papers.background: 멀티모달 대형 언어 모델(MLLM)의 안전성은 후학습 정렬이나 활성화 스티어링에 필요한 위험한 멀티모달 데이터에 크게 의존한다. 그러나 이러한 데이터는 수집이 어렵고, 각 모달마다 새로 모아야 하며, 수집과 배포 과정에서 윤리적·법적 문제가 발생할 수 있다. 이 연구는 멀티모달 안전 데이터 없이 텍스트 거부 방향만으로 안전성을 확보할 수 있는지 탐구한다.
papers.summary: 이 논문은 LLM 백본에서 직접 추출한 텍스트 거부 방향(textual refusal directions)이 이미지·비디오 등 다른 모달로 일반화되는지 확인한다. 이를 기반으로 학습 불필요한 경량 방법인 MARS(Modality-Agnostic Refusal Steering)를 제안하며, 활성화 중심화(activation centering)로 모달 불일치를 보정하고, 기하적으로 정의된 신뢰 영역 내에서 스티어링 강도를 적응적으로 조절하며, 첫 생성 토큰에서 최적 개입 계층을 선택한다. 5개의 최신 SOTA MLLM에서 안전성, 유용성, 비디오 제일브레이크 평가로 검증한 결과, 안전성 향상을 일관되게 달성하면서 유용성을 과도한 거부(over-refusal) 수준까지 보존했다. MARS는 안전 관련 구조가 모달 간 공유되고, 텍스트 거부 방향이 멀티모달 정렬의 강력한 기반임을 보여준다.
papers.limitations: (추정) MARS는 모달 불일치를 보정하지만, 여전히 안전한 멀티모달 입력이 오거부(spurious refusal)로 유도될 가능성이 남을 수 있다. (추정) 텍스트 거부 방향이 LLM 백본에서 추출되므로, 백본의 안전 표현 구조에 의존할 수 있다. (추정) 이미지와 비디오를 중심으로 검증되었기 때문에 다른 멀티모달 입력이나 새로운 공격에는 일반화 성능이 제한될 수 있다.

papers.title: LIBERO-Industry: Benchmarking Robotic Manipulation under Industrial Process Constraints
papers.abstract: Industrial manipulation in flexible manufacturing, e.g., high-mix, low-volume (HMLV) electronics assembly, requires robot policies to adapt to changing products and production conditions. Such settings impose industrial process constraints, including product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. However, existing evaluation frameworks do not systematically capture these constraints when assessing generalist robot policies. To address this gap, we introduce LIBERO-Industry, a novel benchmark built on the widely used robot learning benchmark LIBERO, that translates the aforementioned industrial constraints into controllable task conditions and measurable success criteria. Specifically, LIBERO-Industry comprises three classic task scenarios: Static-to-Dynamic (S2D) loading, Dynamic-to-Static (D2S) unloading, and Dynamic-to-Dynamic (D2D) transfer. The suites contain 216 tasks in total that systematically vary object geometry, conveyor speed, interaction-window duration, and geometric acceptance region size. Extensive experiments across five generalist robot policies (including vision-language-action models and world-action models) show that performance progressively degrades as industrial constraints are introduced and combined. Under a shared fine-tuning and evaluation protocol, the LIBERO-Industry co-training condition achieved higher observed target-transfer completion than the original-LIBERO condition.
papers.organization: Physical AI Group, Institute of AI for Engineering (IAIE), Tongji University
papers.title_ko: LIBERO-Industry: 산업 공정 제약 조건에서의 로봇 조작 벤치마킹
papers.background: 유연 제조, 특히 고혼합·소량(HMLV) 전자 조립과 같은 산업 조작 환경에서는 로봇 정책이 제품과 생산 조건 변화에 적응해야 합니다. 이러한 환경에는 제품 변형, 이동하는 소재 흐름, 유한한 실행 창, 엄격한 기하학적 허용 오차 같은 산업 공정 제약이 존재합니다. 그러나 기존 평가 프레임워크는 범용 로봇 정책을 평가할 때 이러한 제약을 체계적으로 반영하지 못합니다.
papers.summary: 본 연구는 널리 쓰이는 로봇 학습 벤치마크 LIBERO를 기반으로 산업 공정 제약을 제어 가능한 작업 조건과 측정 가능한 성공 기준으로 변환한 LIBERO-Industry를 제안합니다. 이 벤치마크는 정적-동적(S2D) 적재, 동적-정적(D2S) 하역, 동적-동적(D2D) 이송이라는 세 가지 시나리오로 구성되며, 216개 작업에서 객체 기하, 컨베이어 속도, 상호작용 창 길이, 기하학적 허용 영역 크기를 체계적으로 변화시킵니다. 다섯 가지 범용 로봇 정책을 대상으로 한 실험에서는 산업 제약이 도입되고 결합될수록 성능이 점진적으로 저하되는 것으로 나타났습니다. 동일한 파인튜닝 및 평가 프로토콜에서 LIBERO-Industry 공동 학습(co-training) 조건은 기존 LIBERO 조건보다 더 높은 관측된 대상 이전(target-transfer) 완료율을 보였습니다.
papers.limitations: (추정) LIBERO 기반 시뮬레이션 환경에 구축되어 있어 실제 산업 현장의 하드웨어, 센서 노이즈, 안전 제약 등을 완전히 반영하지 못할 수 있습니다. (추정) 세 가지 시나리오와 216개 작업으로 구성되어 있어 다양한 산업 공정, 장기 작업, 더 넓은 제품 변형 범위를 충분히 커버하지 못할 수 있습니다. (추정) 결과 해석이 공유된 파인튜닝 및 평가 프로토콜과 특정 이전 완료율 지표에 의존하므로, 다른 학습·평가 설정으로의 일반화는 제한적일 수 있습니다.

papers.title: Remembering Has a Price: Learning Memory Worth under Resource Constraints
papers.abstract: Lifelong agents continually accumulate and reuse experience to improve after deployment, yet in practice they often operate under tight generation, interaction, and memory budgets. Under such stringent joint constraints, we find that existing lifelong-memory methods can become ineffective, with several sophisticated approaches offering little advantage over simple retrieval or even no-memory agents. This reveals a more fundamental problem: resource scarcity makes each memory decision more consequential. When only a small amount of past experience can be retained or reused and opportunities for reasoning and recovery are limited, retrieving a relevant but ineffective memory can consume scarce context and hinder downstream execution. The key challenge is therefore not simply to retrieve relevant experience, but to determine which experiences are actually worth retaining and reusing. To address this challenge, we propose TokenWorth, a lightweight online memory framework that learns query-dependent memory worth from sparse execution feedback and applies it consistently to memory retrieval and bounded memory management. Across three LifelongAgentBench environments and both local and API-based deployments, TokenWorth achieves the highest task success rate while using the fewest output tokens among the evaluated methods. These results suggest that effective lifelong adaptation under resource constraints depends not on remembering more, but on learning what is worth remembering. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/AIGNLAI/TokenWorth.
papers.title_ko: 기억에는 대가가 있다: 자원 제약 하에서의 기억 가치 학습
papers.background: 평생 에이전트(lifelong agents)는 배포 이후에도 경험을 계속 축적하고 재사용하여 성능을 개선하지만, 실제에서는 생성, 상호작용, 메모리 예산이 모두 엄격하게 제한되는 경우가 많다. 이러한 복합 제약 하에서는 기존 평생 메모리 방법들이 단순 검색이나 메모리 없는 에이전트보다 큰 이점을 보이지 못할 수 있다. 따라서 핵심 문제는 단순히 관련 경험을 찾는 것이 아니라, 제한된 자원 안에서 어떤 경험을 유지하고 재사용할 가치가 있는지를 판단하는 것이다.
papers.summary: 본 논문은 희박한 실행 피드백에서 쿼리 의존적 기억 가치(query-dependent memory worth)를 학습하는 경량 온라인 메모리 프레임워크 TokenWorth를 제안한다. 학습된 기억 가치는 메모리 검색과 제한된 메모리 관리에 일관되게 적용된다. 세 가지 LifelongAgentBench 환경과 로컬/API 기반 배포에서 TokenWorth는 평가된 방법 중 가장 높은 작업 성공률을 달성하면서 가장 적은 출력 토큰을 사용했다. 이는 자원 제약 하의 효과적인 평생 적응이 더 많이 기억하는 것이 아니라, 기억할 가치가 있는 것을 학습하는 데 달려 있음을 시사한다.
papers.limitations: (추정) 평가가 세 가지 LifelongAgentBench 환경과 로컬/API 배포에 한정되어 있어, 다른 작업 도메인이나 더 긴 시간축의 평생 환경에서의 일반화 가능성은 확인되지 않는다. (추정) 희박한 실행 피드백에 의존하므로 초기 단계나 피드백이 매우 드문 환경에서는 기억 가치 학습이 느리거나 불안정할 수 있다. (추정) 출력 토큰 효율과 작업 성공률에 초점을 두고 있어, 메모리 내용 자체의 정확성이나 장기적 지식 축적의 세부적 품질은 초록만으로는 판단하기 어렵다.

papers.title: Learning to Discriminate Scene Structures Makes Self-Supervised Depth Learning Scalable
papers.abstract: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation is appealing for its potential to scale with unlabeled data, yet existing methods often degrade when trained on diverse scenes. This study finds that, under self-supervision, models tend to encode dataset-specific structural biases rather than transferable scene geometry, leading to cross-domain optimization conflicts. To address this issue, this study proposes the MaSS framework, aiming to make self-supervised depth learning scalable to diverse data. MaSS introduces a dedicated structural representation pathway explicitly decoupled from contextual features, which is guided by a novel scene-structure discrimination objective to learn generalized, layout-aware structural representations for depth decoding. Trained and evaluated on four diverse datasets, both individually and jointly, MaSS substantially outperforms prior self-supervised methods and is the first to consistently benefit from mixed-domain training. Zero-shot evaluation on eight additional datasets further demonstrates its remarkable generalizability, particularly on those entirely out-of-distribution scenes. The source code is publicly available at https://mias.group/MaSS.
papers.title_ko: 장면 구조를 구분하는 학습이 자기지도적 깊이 학습의 확장성을 높인다
papers.background: 자기지도적 단안 깊이 추정(self-supervised monocular depth estimation)은 비지표 데이터를 활용해 확장할 수 있다는 점에서 매력적이지만, 다양한 장면으로 훈련 시 기존 방법들의 성능이 저하되는 문제가 있다. 이 연구는 자기지도 학습 하에서 모델이 전이 가능한 장면 기하학(scene geometry) 대신 데이터셋 특유의 구조적 편향을 학습하는 경향이 있어, 도메인 간 최적화 충돌이 발생한다고 지적한다.
papers.summary: 본 연구는 다양한 데이터로 확장 가능한 자기지도적 깊이 학습을 위해 MaSS 프레임워크를 제안한다. MaSS는 문맥적 특징(contextual features)과 명시적으로 분리된 전용 구조 표현 경로를 도입하고, 새로운 장면 구조 판별(scene-structure discrimination) 목적함수로 일반화 가능하고 레이아웃을 인지하는 구조 표현을 학습해 깊이 해독에 활용한다. 4가지 다양한 데이터셋에서 개별 및 혼합 훈련으로 평가한 결과, 기존 자기지도적 방법보다 크게 우수한 성능을 보였으며, 혼합 도메인 훈련에서 일관되게 이점을 얻은 첫 사례이다. 8개의 추가 데이터셋에 대한 제로샷 평가에서는 특히 분포 외(out-of-distribution) 장면에서 뛰어난 일반화 가능성을 보였다.
papers.limitations: (추정) 자기지도적 단안 깊이 추정 방식은 실제 깊이 지표를 사용하지 않으므로, 절대 깊이 정확도나 정밀한 스케일 추정에 한계가 있을 수 있다. (추정) 장면 구조 판별 목적과 별도의 구조 표현 경로를 추가하기 때문에 학습 및 추론 비용이 증가할 수 있다. (추정) 8개 추가 데이터셋의 제로샷 평가로 일반화 가능성을 보였지만, 모든 분포 외 장면이나 실시간 적용까지 검증한 것은 아니다.

papers.title: Self-Evaluating Recursive Agents
papers.abstract: Recursive language-model agents decompose tasks and delegate subtasks to child instances of the same policy, forming a tree of work. Training them, however, is hard: the final outcome is verifiable, but the self-invented intermediate subtasks are numerous and carry no ground truth. Existing methods score each node with a verifier or judge, which is costly at scale and blind to decomposition quality. We argue that a recursive agent must learn three coupled capabilities within one set of weights: decomposing problems into subtasks, solving them, and evaluating the outcomes, each requiring its own training signal. SERA (Self-Evaluating Recursive Agents) turns evaluation into a learned capability of the policy itself. Before delegating, the parent writes a rubric of weighted success criteria for each child subtask; a ranking objective against verified outcomes then trains rubric generation so that the criteria track genuine subtask success. In addition, a complementary leaf-coverage signal provides direct credit for task decomposition. Our central finding is that training the policy to generate aligned rubrics is what drives the gains: because the same weights both evaluate and execute, learning to judge subtasks sharpens the agent's ability to solve them. Notably, external supervision is also reduced: the judge is consulted only to train the rubric generator, while solving is trained against the agent's own rubric scores, which outperform direct use of the judge. Beyond training, the learned rubric doubles as an inference-time selector for tree search. On TextCraft-Synth and TextWorld-Sync, SERA improves over strong recursive-agent baselines by 5.38 and 13.14 points on average, and rubric-guided tree search at inference adds a further 2.43 points on TextWorld-Sync.
papers.title_ko: 자기 평가형 재귀 에이전트
papers.background: 재귀 언어모델 에이전트는 작업을 분해하고 같은 정책의 자식 인스턴스에 하위 작업을 위임해 작업 트리를 형성한다. 그러나 최종 결과만 검증 가능하고, 스스로 만든 중간 하위 작업은 많지만 정답 기준이 없어 학습이 어렵다. 기존 방법은 검증기나 판정기로 각 노드를 평가하지만 대규모에서는 비용이 크고 분해 품질을 놓친다.
papers.summary: SERA는 평가 자체를 정책이 학습하는 능력으로 전환한다. 부모 에이전트가 하위 작업 위임 전에 가중 성공 기준을 포함한 평가 기준(rubric)을 작성하고, 검증된 결과와의 랭킹 목적함수로 rubric 생성을 학습해 기준이 실제 하위 작업 성공을 추적하도록 한다. 보완적인 leaf-coverage 신호는 작업 분해에 직접적인 크레딧을 제공한다. 학습된 rubric은 추론 시 트리 탐색의 선택자로도 활용되며, TextCraft-Synth와 TextWorld-Sync에서 강력한 재귀 에이전트 대비 각각 평균 5.38점과 13.14점 개선하고, TextWorld-Sync에서 rubric 기반 트리 탐색이 추가로 2.43점을 더한다.
papers.limitations: (추정) rubric 학습에 검증된 결과가 필요하므로 최종 결과를 신뢰할 수 있게 검증하기 어려운 영역에서는 적용이 제한될 수 있다. (추정) rubric 생성과 rubric 기반 트리 탐색은 추론 비용과 시스템 복잡도를 높일 수 있다. (추정) 같은 가중치가 평가와 실행을 모두 담당하므로 자기 평가 편향이나 기준에 대한 과도한 최적화가 발생할 가능성이 있다.

papers.title: StopLoss: Teaching Agents to Predict Failure and Stop Early
papers.abstract: Coding agents keep working on runs that will fail verification, and asking a frontier model to watch for this is expensive in its own right. We introduce StopLoss, a small external monitor that learns failure recognition from completed trajectories and their verifier outcomes. The name is inspired by the stop-loss order in finance: StopLoss ends a run early when the run is likely to fail, which saves resources. Final outcomes label earlier local windows, so a fine-tuned language model can score the most recent tool steps in a single forward pass, and a threshold calibrated on successful runs turns that score into an abort decision without changing the executor. Trained on GPT-family SWE-rebench trajectories and evaluated on SWE-bench Verified and a SWE-bench Pro subset with GPT and Claude executors, StopLoss is compared against six general-purpose judges reading identical windows. Outcome supervision lifts failure prediction from near chance to a useful signal at the first check, at one to two orders of magnitude lower cost per check than any tested judge. This translates into savings: relative to completing every task, StopLoss lowers cost per retained solve by 4.5\% on Verified while preserving 99\% of successful runs, and by up to 31\% on the costlier Pro subset, reaching 48\% with a Qwen3-8B backbone, and in all four settings its cost per retained solve is below that of every judge policy. Outcome-trained small monitors can make failure recognition cheap enough for early stopping to pay for itself.
papers.title_ko: StopLoss: 에이전트가 실패를 예측하고 조기에 중단하도록 학습하기
papers.background: 코딩 에이전트(coding agent)는 검증(verification)에 실패할 실행을 계속 수행하는 경우가 많아 자원 낭비가 발생한다. 프런티어 모델(frontier model)에 실패 감시를 맡기면 모니터링 비용이 추가로 커진다. 따라서 실행 도중 실패 가능성을 저렴하게 판단해 조기에 중단하는 장치가 필요하다.
papers.summary: StopLoss는 완료된 궤적(trajectory)과 검증기(verifier) 결과를 이용해 실패를 인식하는 소형 외부 모니터를 제안한다. 최종 결과가 이전의 짧은 윈도우를 라벨링하므로, 파인튜닝된 언어 모델이 최근 도구 단계(tool step)만 한 번의 전방 전파(forward pass)로 점수화하고, 성공 실행에서 보정된 임계값으로 실행기를 변경하지 않고 중단 여부를 결정한다. GPT 계열 SWE-rebench 궤적으로 학습하고 SWE-bench Verified와 Pro 부분집합에서 GPT·Claude 실행기로 평가한 결과, 첫 검사 시 실패 예측이 무작위 수준에서 유용한 신호로 향상됐고, 검사당 비용은 테스트된 판정 모델보다 1~2개 자릿수 낮았다. 모든 설정에서 유지된 성공 건당 비용이 6개 일반 목적 판정 모델보다 낮았으며, Verified에서는 성공 실행의 99%를 유지하면서 4.5% 절감하고, Pro 부분집합에서는 최대 31%, Qwen3-8B 기반에서는 48% 절감했다.
papers.limitations: (추정) GPT 계열 SWE-bench 계열 궤적으로 학습되어 다른 도메인, 실행기, 도구 환경에서는 성능이 달라질 수 있다. (추정) 검증기 결과와 성공 실행 기반 임계값에 의존하므로 검증 신호가 불완전하거나 실패 분포가 바뀌면 조기 중단 판단이 불안정해질 수 있다. (추정) 최근 도구 단계만 점수화하는 방식이라 장기적 의존성이나 미묘한 실패 징후를 놓칠 수 있다.

papers.title: Policy Is Not Capability: Some Safety Benchmarks Measure Which Definition of "Unsafe" You Trained On
papers.abstract: A guardrail classifier is reported as if unsafe were a property of text. It is not: it is a property of a policy, and the policy enters the model through its labels. We exploit an accident of an industrial deployment in which the same ~53k prompts were labelled twice, under two operational definitions ("is this a request for harmful content?" and "would a moderator block this?"), and used to train ten guardrail arms sharing architecture, codebase and optimiser family, at two model scales. First, the guardrail's own training corpus already contained the benchmarks: JailbreakBench-benign is 88% and OR-Bench-hard 82% present in the training pools, two over-refusal benchmarks, the kind a guardrail reports to argue it does not over-block. Everything below is decontaminated. Second, safety benchmarks stratify sharply by how much of their score is decided by the label definition rather than by the model: with architecture and optimiser fixed, the range across the ten arms is 0.99 on HarmBench-copyright and 0.043 on WildGuard-benign, a 23x spread. Third, a benchmark score can be moved across its entire range by 0.03% of the parameters. Across these arms HarmBench-copyright spans 0-100 and OR-Bench-hard over-refusal 3.4-56.4%, and the four arms whose last supervision signal carries a given policy occupy one extreme of both (exact rank p=0.005, or 0.04-0.14 at worst), at unchanged detection capability. For a distilled student the teacher's soft labels do this even when every hard label carries the other policy, so teacher provenance is an unrecorded confound in any released checkpoint. Fourth, validation accuracy on the one split that grades all twenty arms tracks agreement with the annotator's policy (rho=+0.74), not detection capability (rho=+0.34). We argue that guardrail evaluations should report contamination, a seed floor and the definition they were graded against as first-class variables.
papers.title_ko: 정책은 역량이 아니다: 일부 안전 벤치마크는 '안전하지 않음'의 어떤 정의를 학습했는지를 측정한다
papers.background: 가드레일 분류기는 텍스트 자체의 속성인 것처럼 '안전하지 않음'을 측정하는 것으로 보고되지만, 실제로는 라벨에 담긴 정책(policy)의 속성에 가깝다. 기존 안전 벤치마크는 학습 데이터 오염과 라벨 정의 차이를 구분하지 못해, 모델의 실제 탐지 역량을 과대 또는 과소 평가할 수 있다. 이 연구는 동일한 프롬프트가 두 가지 운영 정의 아래 이중 라벨링된 산업 배포 사례를 활용해 이 문제를 분석한다.
papers.summary: 연구팀은 약 53k 프롬프트를 '유해 콘텐츠 요청인가'와 '모더레이터가 차단할 것인가'라는 두 정의로 라벨링하고, 같은 구조·코드베이스·옵티마이저 계열의 10개 가드레일 모델을 두 규모로 학습했다. JailbreakBench-benign의 88%와 OR-Bench-hard의 82%가 학습 풀에 이미 포함되어 있음을 확인한 뒤, 모든 평가를 오염 제거(decontamination) 상태로 수행했다. 벤치마크 점수는 모델 역량보다 라벨 정의에 따라 크게 달라졌고, 전체 점수 범위를 0.03%의 파라미터 변화만으로 이동시킬 수 있었으며, 마지막 감독 신호의 정책이 점수 극단부를 결정했다. 증류 학생 모델에서는 교사의 소프트 라벨이 모든 하드 라벨이 다른 정책을 담고 있어도 영향을 미쳤고, 검증 정확도는 탐지 역량보다 주석자 정책 일치도와 더 강하게 상관되어, 평가 시 오염·시드 하한·채점 정의를 1급 변수로 보고해야 한다고 주장한다.
papers.limitations: (추정) 특정 산업 배포와 10개 가드레일 암, 두 모델 규모에 기반하므로 다른 모델 계열, 규모, 또는 실제 운영 정책에서는 결과가 일반화되지 않을 수 있다. (추정) 벤치마크 오염 제거와 선택된 안전 벤치마크에 초점을 두어, 오염의 전체 범위나 실시간 정책 변화, 더 넓은 안전 역량을 포착하지 못할 수 있다. (추정) 가드레일 분류기의 벤치마크 점수 해석에 집중하므로, 실제 차단 정책 설계나 사용자 경험에 대한 직접적 개선 방안은 제시하지 않는다.

papers.title: ECHO: Efficient Causal Self-Recursion Beyond Auxiliary Multi-Token Prediction
papers.abstract: Existing Multi-token prediction (MTP) methods are auxiliary by design: the multi-horizon loss mostly trains modules attached to the backbone, and each added horizon costs another module and another pass. We propose Efficient Causal Self-Recursion (ECHO), which removes both costs. The backbone's own final layer predicts every horizon, so the supervision lands on the parameters that generate the next token, and Dynamic Depth Sampling (DDS) keeps deeper horizons affordable by drawing the training depth with probabilities that decay along depth. Future prediction thus becomes part of the autoregressive objective rather than a task attached to it, and the gains follow on both sides of it. In pretraining, added depth converts into downstream accuracy where auxiliary modules saturate, concentrating on reasoning and code at half the MTP training overhead of training every depth. At inference, the pretrained model is its own drafter: it drafts beyond the depth it was trained for, and keeps its draft-target alignment on the open-ended, high-entropy generation where post-hoc drafters lose theirs. The advantage survives a doubled token budget, a repeated pretraining run, and supervised finetuning.
papers.title_ko: ECHO: 보조 다중 토큰 예측을 넘어선 효율적 인과 자기 재귀
papers.background: 기존 다중 토큰 예측(MTP) 방식은 본질적으로 보조 모듈에 의존하며, 멀티호라이즌 손실이 백본이 아닌 부착된 모듈을 주로 학습시킨다. 이로 인해 예측 지평을 늘릴 때마다 추가 모듈과 추가 전파 비용이 발생하고, 다음 토큰 생성에 직접 관여하는 백본 파라미터에 학습 신호가 충분히 전달되지 않는 문제가 있다.
papers.summary: ECHO는 백본의 최종 레이어가 모든 예측 지평을 직접 예측하도록 하여, 미래 예측을 자율 회귀 목표의 일부로 통합한다. 동적 깊이 샘플링(DDS)은 깊이에 따라 확률이 감소하는 방식으로 학습 깊이를 추출해 깊은 지평의 학습 비용을 낮춘다. 사전학습에서는 추가 깊이가 보조 모듈이 포화되는 영역에서 다운스트림 정확도로 전환되어, 특히 추론과 코드에서 모든 깊이를 학습하는 MTP 대비 절반의 학습 오버헤드로 이점을 보인다. 추론 시에는 사전학습된 모델이 자체 드래프터로 동작해 학습된 깊이보다 멀리 드래프트하고, 개방형·고엔트로피 생성에서 사후 드래프터보다 드래프트-타깃 정합성을 유지하며, 토큰 예산 2배, 반복 사전학습, SFT에서도 이점이 유지된다.
papers.limitations: (추정) ECHO는 백본 최종 레이어가 모든 지평을 예측해야 하므로, 깊은 지평을 사용할 때 여전히 메모리나 계산 부담이 발생할 수 있다. (추정) 동적 깊이 샘플링은 확률적으로 깊이를 선택하므로, 깊은 지평의 학습이 충분히 이루어지지 않거나 감소 확률 설정에 민감할 수 있다. (추정) 초록은 추론·코드와 자체 드래프팅 이점을 강조하지만, 모든 도메인이나 다른 생성 방식까지 동일한 이점을 보장하지는 않는다.

papers.title: Progress-Aware Distillation for Mitigating Stagnation in Small Language Model Agents
papers.abstract: While LLM-based agent systems have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in reasoning and solving complex real-world tasks, they also come with substantial token consumption and inference latency, limiting their practical deployment. To enhance the efficiency of agent systems, recent efforts have focused on transferring agentic capabilities from large-scale models to small language models (SLMs) via supervised fine-tuning-based distillation. Nevertheless, as interaction trajectories grow longer, involving extended reasoning-action chains and extensive environmental feedback, distilled student agents tend to experience progress stagnation: becoming trapped in unproductive loops characterized by persistent failed strategies and difficulty making meaningful progress. Our systematic analysis shows that this phenomenon consistently occurs across diverse SLMs and task domains. To address this issue, we propose Progress-Aware Distillation (ProD), which explicitly detects and penalizes stagnation in student-generated trajectories. ProD encodes the stagnation gap between student and teacher into an adaptive margin for dynamically penalizing possible stagnation. By iteratively applying this procedure, ProD enables student agents to progressively approximate teacher behavior. Extensive experiments involving 8 SLMs, ranging from 0.6B to 8B parameters, on both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, demonstrate that ProD substantially mitigates progress stagnation while enhancing both the success rates and task-completion efficiency of distilled SLM agents.
papers.title_ko: 작은 언어 모델 에이전트의 정체 현상 완화를 위한 진전 인식 증류
papers.background: LLM 기반 에이전트 시스템은 복잡한 실제 작업에서 뛰어난 성능을 보이지만, 높은 토큰 소비와 추론 지연으로 실용적 배포가 제한된다. 대규모 모델의 에이전트 능력을 작은 언어 모델로 이전하기 위해 감독 미세 조정 기반 증류가 시도되고 있다. 그러나 추론-행동 체인과 환경 피드백이 긴 궤적으로 확장되면, 학생 에이전트는 실패한 전략에 갇혀 의미 있는 진전을 하지 못하는 정체 현상을 겪는다.
papers.summary: 본 연구는 학생이 생성한 궤적에서 정체를 명시적으로 감지하고 페널티를 부과하는 Progress-Aware Distillation(ProD)을 제안한다. ProD는 학생과 교사 간 정체 간극을 적응적 마진으로 인코딩해 잠재적 정체를 동적으로 처벌한다. 이 과정을 반복적으로 적용하면 학생 에이전트가 교사 동작에 점진적으로 근사한다. 0.6B~8B 매개변수의 8개 SLM을 대상으로 한 도메인 내외 벤치마크 실험에서 ProD는 정체 현상을 완화하고 성공률과 작업 완료 효율을 향상시켰다.
papers.limitations: (추정) 초록은 8개 SLM과 특정 벤치마크에 대한 결과만 제시하므로, 더 다양한 모델 규모나 실제 배포 환경에서의 일반화 효과는 확인되지 않는다. (추정) 정체 간극을 적응적 마진으로 변환하고 반복 증류를 수행하는 방식은 추가적인 계산 비용이나 튜닝 부담을 초래할 수 있다.

papers.title: A Conditional No-Hair Theorem for Transformers: How Language Models Forget Their Prompt
papers.abstract: We ask how much an autoregressive transformer retains of its prompt after generating t tokens. Consider two different prompts followed by the same continuation text, so that any difference in their hidden states comes from the prompt alone, and we find that the distance between their hidden states decays approximately as a power law t^{-α}, where α=1 is the rate at which a fixed prompt's share of uniform attention shrinks and smaller values mean longer memory. Trained models forget fast (αapprox0.55--0.7), untrained ones slowly (αapprox0.2--0.5). We prove that this offset is Obig(P(log t)^{L-1}/tbig) for a prompt of length P and depth L. The bound holds for finite-depth pre-LN softmax transformers with bounded attention logits, under one additional condition: the pre-norm activations stay away from zero. The mechanism is geometric: the prompt's direct influence is diluted as the context grows, and relay --- continuation tokens passing on what earlier tokens read from the prompt --- can only add logarithmic factors. This is what we call the conditional no-hair theorem: given the text generated so far, the prompt's influence on the next token vanishes as t grows, so any property of the prompt that survives, such as its language, must be carried by the text itself. An exactly solvable linear relay model shows that the bound cannot be improved and reproduces the rise of the local exponent towards 1 seen in untrained networks. Cancelling the dilution with a logit bias stops the decay early in training and reverses it after, so dilution is necessary for the forgetting we measure; untrained networks and the solvable model show it is also sufficient.
papers.title_ko: 트랜스포머에 대한 조건부 무모(No-Hair) 정리: 언어 모델은 어떻게 프롬프트를 잊는가
papers.background: 자기회귀형 트랜스포머가 토큰을 생성하면서 원래 프롬프트의 영향을 얼마나 유지하는지, 즉 언어 모델의 프롬프트 기억과 망각을 정량적으로 이해하는 것이 문제이다. 특히 동일한 후속 텍스트를 이은 서로 다른 프롬프트가 hidden state에 남기는 차이는 프롬프트 자체의 영향만으로 해석할 수 있어, 생성 토큰 수 t에 따른 영향 감소율을 분석할 수 있다. 이 연구는 프롬프트 정보가 다음 토큰 예측에 얼마나 오래 남는지, 그리고 어떤 조건에서 사라지는지를 묻는다.
papers.summary: 연구자는 서로 다른 프롬프트 뒤에 동일한 continuation text를 연결하여 hidden state 차이를 프롬프트만의 효과로 분리하고, 이 차이가 t의 -α제곱으로 감소함을 분석한다. 학습된 모델은 α≈0.55~0.7로 빠르게 잊고, 학습되지 않은 모델은 α≈0.2~0.5로 더 오래 기억하는 것으로 나타났다. 프롬프트 길이 P, 깊이 L인 유한 깊이 pre-LN softmax 트랜스포머에서 이 차이는 O(P(log t)^(L-1)/t)로 상한을 가지며, 정확히 풀 수 있는 선형 relay 모델이 이 상한이 최적임을 보이고, logit bias로 dilution을 상쇄하면 초기 학습에서 감소가 멈추고 이후 역전되어 dilution이 측정된 망각의 핵심 요인임을 시사한다. 이는 조건부 무모 정리로, 이미 생성된 텍스트가 주어지면 t가 커질수록 프롬프트의 직접적 영향은 사라지고, 프롬프트의 언어 등 잔존 속성은 생성 텍스트 자체에 의해 전달되어야 함을 의미한다.
papers.limitations: 이론적 경계는 유한 깊이 pre-LN softmax 트랜스포머, 제한된 어텐션 로짓, 그리고 pre-norm activations가 0에서 벗어나야 한다는 조건에서 성립한다. (추정) post-LN, 무제한 로짓, 무한 깊이, 또는 다른 어텐션 메커니즘을 포함한 실제 대규모 모델까지 일반화되지는 않을 수 있다. (추정) logit bias 등으로 dilution을 상쇄하면 망각이 멈추거나 역전될 수 있어, 실제 프롬프트 정보 보존이나 유출 평가에는 이 조건이 충족되는지 확인이 필요하다.

papers.title: UniAVC: Unified Audio-Video Creation via Progressive Training and Asymmetric Scheduling
papers.abstract: Unified audio-video creation requires a single model capable of text-conditioned joint synthesis, bidirectional cross-modal generation, and instruction-guided editing across both modalities. Existing methods rely heavily on paired corpora, which are scarce for joint generation and even rarer for editing. Consequently, they are spent learning single-branch generative and editing capabilities that abundant unimodal data could readily teach, rather than on the cross-modal coupling. Furthermore, prevailing systems apply a single shared noise schedule to both modalities, neglecting two critical limitations. First, due to the significant discrepancy in information density, video requires prolonged high noise to organize spatial and motion structure, whereas the sparser audio signal can settle earlier during the synthesis process, the dynamics a uniform schedule might compromise. Second, lockstep denoising leaves asymmetric workflows, such as conditioning on one modality to synthesize or edit another, untrained. We present UniAVC, which addresses both obstacles. It first trains each branch on unimodal dataset to full generative and editing competence, and subsequently dedicates paired data to exploit cross-modal correspondence. Modality-decoupled schedulers meanwhile warp the noise schedule independently from a shared timestep, while subtasks with one clean modality directly supervise asymmetric configurations. These settings respectively enable intent-aware editing, which preserves one modality intact while enlisting it to constrain the other, and post-inference self-refinement, which regenerates only an unsatisfactory branch against an accepted one. UniAVC thus spans multiple creation tasks from a single set of weights without task-specific adapters.

papers.title: Competing Learning in Hybrid Architectures
papers.abstract: Many modern language models have adopted hybrid architectures that incorporate both linear-time recurrence and softmax attention. Modern recurrence layers provide a highly expressive mixing mechanism while ensuring high throughput by compressing contextual information into a fixed-size state, but underperform softmax attention in contextual information retrieval. In this paper, we reveal a Competing Learning phenomenon where different kinds of mixers compete to learn the same function, and when any layer learns a function, it suppresses the corresponding learning signal for other layers. Layer attribution analysis reveals that under typical data distributions, modern recurrence learns retrieval functions faster than softmax attention, causing attention to fail to learn retrieval in most cases. Stopping weight updates in recurrence in the middle of training helps attention learn retrieval. Based on these results, we propose a staged training procedure for pre-training hybrid architectures on natural language. Empirical results on models up to 1B parameters show that our method results in substantial improvement in language modeling loss, common-sense reasoning, as well as a wide range of retrieval-related tasks across different context lengths.

papers.title: Factorization-Guided Training and Inference for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference through parallel verification of tokens proposed by a drafter. Diffusion drafters further parallelize proposal generation, but greater proposal capacity or higher mean accepted tokens (MAT) need not yield higher throughput. Because verification accepts only a consecutive prefix, early rejections can render later correct predictions ineffective, limiting MAT gains, while even higher MAT may not improve throughput if per-round latency increases. We introduce DScout, which uses two complementary factorizations to guide diffusion drafter training and inference for higher throughput. For training, DScout factorizes position-wise loss into inclusion, weighting, and prediction loss. This guides the design and combination of mixed-horizon training, intra-block unmasking, and acceptance-weighted loss to align supervision with prefix acceptance and improve MAT. For inference, DScout factorizes throughput as the ratio of MAT to per-round latency, guiding target-conditioning depth, drafter depth, and inference block size selection to identify a high-throughput configuration for each workload. Across six benchmarks, DScout achieves 3.84times and 4.14times mean speedups over autoregressive decoding on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, respectively, improving mean speedup over the state-of-the-art baseline by 9.1% and 7.1%. Across models and concurrency settings, our inference configuration policy provides up to 9.75% additional mean speedup over DScout's fixed configuration.

papers.title: Co-Evolving Acting and Forecasting for Language Agents
papers.abstract: Training language agents is bottlenecked by the high cost of long-horizon rollouts, yet standard agentic reinforcement learning (RL) learns only from a terminal scalar reward, leaving the supervision in intermediate steps largely unused. Prior work exploits this supervision through value targets that estimate per-step success probabilities or observation targets that fit environment response. Both are hard to construct well: (1) value targets come from the same single scalar signal for each step in the trajectory, and (2) observation targets, such as web pages and terminal logs, are long and noisy and reach only one step ahead. We propose CoPE, which adds a third kind of multi-step action targets. On successful on-policy trajectories, CoPE trains the policy backbone to generate the action sequences that follows each history. Each action is also supervised when forecast from the preceding histories, forming a temporal ensemble that the shared backbone absorbs during training, and this enables acting and forecasting to co-evolve. The policy still acts one step at a time at inference, with no overhead. Across five benchmarks (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, τ^2-bench, and AppWorld), CoPE (1) achieves stronger aggregate performance than GRPO and RL baselines with predictive auxiliary targets across simulated environments, while improving overall performance on both realistic applications; (2) delivers up to 1.9times and 2.0times higher sample efficiency than ECHO and GRPO, respectively, on ScienceWorld; and (3) achieves these gains with a single policy backbone, without additional models, separate pretraining, or inference overhead. The codebase is available at https://github.com/ulab-uiuc/CoPE.

papers.title: World Model Interpretability: From Decoding Representations to Understanding Latent Worlds
papers.abstract: Emerging Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are moving beyond representation learning towards latent world models that support prediction, planning, and control. Yet their latent worlds naturally lack a human-interpretable interface. In this Perspective, we argue that as JEPA latents become internal states for prediction and action, interpretability must move beyond what they encode to how latent variables interact, evolve, and causally drive prediction. To this end, we envision a four-stage research agenda, involving Ground, Structure, Verify, and Act, to guide this shift toward actionable latent-world understanding. Within our framework, existing JEPA interpretability efforts provide early evidence for Ground, while systematic analysis of latent structure, causal verification, and intervention remains largely unexplored. Overall, this Perspective aims to call for a broader latent-world interpretability agenda that shifts attention from decoding representations toward understanding, validating, and acting on latent worlds.

papers.title: N-Gram Memories at Two Bits: Quantizing Lookup Tables in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Conditional memory expands language-model capacity through selective lookup, but the full embedding table must remain available for every possible input. We introduce Conditional Program (CP), a compressed representation that reconstructs only the rows an input requests. CP represents each row by a short code and a local scale, with a reconstruction program shared across the table. We instantiate this representation with a Gaussian trellis, norm restoration and independently decodable row records. CP's two-bit code lowers output KL by 41--63\% relative to 2-bit round-to-nearest. Analysis across three trained n-gram memory families shows that Gaussian-like coordinate statistics coexist with learned relationships among rows; at matched storage budgets, the shared trellis outperforms the fitted codebooks and low-rank residual variants we test. For DeepSeek, it reduces table storage from 203GB to 51GB, leaving room for larger workloads when the table is kept on GPU.

papers.title: HandsOn: A Large-Scale Simulation Benchmark for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: General-purpose manipulation requires reliable behavior across embodiments, objects, and task demands. We introduce HandsOn, a composable simulation platform and benchmark for cross-embodiment dexterous manipulation. It supports five robotic arms, six dexterous hands, and approximately 200 rigid, articulated, and deformable assets in randomized scenes. The benchmark pairs 18,000 curated human demonstrations with 66 human-verified tasks: Core-50 supports demonstration-based learning and execution tests, while Transfer-16 evaluates asset and relation transfer, skill composition, and deformable manipulation without target-task training demonstrations. Qualitative real-robot rollouts illustrate sim-to-real transfer. Across diffusion, vision-language-action, world-action, and prompted VLM-based methods, the best trained multi-task policy achieves 29.1% Core-50 success. Without benchmark finetuning, GPT-6 using move_eef for palm-and-finger control achieves 5.2% on Core-50 and 1.9% on Transfer-16 over 660 trials. Trained-policy stage diagnostics expose failures in contact establishment, action coordination, and maintaining achieved goals, with additional sequencing errors in composed tasks. HandsOn provides a shared basis for investigating manipulation generalization and the limits of reliable physical interaction.

papers.title: HSPR: Recovering Software-Agent Benchmark Scores via Hierarchical Posterior Inference
papers.abstract: Evaluating software agents on a full benchmark is expensive. A small task subset can preserve agent rankings while yielding inaccurate scores. Historical responses provide useful structure, but tasks with identical source responses can have different outcomes for a new target agent. We introduce Hierarchical Score Posterior Recovery (HSPR), which combines source-fitted response factors with uncertain group success rates. Observed target outcomes update the posteriors over the target latent state and group rates; posterior-guided acquisition selects subsequent tasks. Its score-based criterion equals the expected one-step reduction in full-score posterior variance. Observed successes and posterior-predictive counts for unqueried tasks yield a full-score posterior. The final estimate uses its median with source-selected calibration. At a 10% task budget on four task banks from the SWE-bench family, HSPR achieves the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) on three banks and the lowest maximum absolute error (MaxErr) on all four among the methods compared. Removing group uncertainty or replacing adaptive queries increases macro MAE in the respective controls. Macro MAE decreases across 5-20% budgets.

papers.title: Predicting Privileged Information Effectiveness for On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enables large language models (LLMs) to learn from privileged information (PI) without a separate teacher model. However, prior work largely treats PI as a fixed design choice, leaving the effects of its content and construction poorly understood. This challenge is particularly important in multi-turn agentic settings, where trajectories contain actions, observations, and reasoning that can be transformed into PI in many ways. We systematically evaluate 16 PI configurations across three multi-turn agentic benchmarks and three student models that vary in scale and reasoning mode. We find that PI effectiveness depends on its content, generation source, and the student model. Information-dense trajectories and PI produced by more capable generators generally yield larger gains, whereas thinking models benefit less consistently. To assess PI before training, we compare PI utility with two KL-based metrics: sampled-token reverse KL (D) and error-step KL contrast (Δd^{-}_{err}). The KL-based metrics track post-training performance more consistently than PI utility, which can be distorted by information leakage. Empirically, selecting each task's PI by Δd^{-}_{err} also improves post-training performance over random selection, most when the PI candidates differ widely. Finally, effective PI remains beneficial when combined with GRPO, allowing the combined objective to outperform a strong GRPO baseline. Overall, our results provide practical guidance for constructing and evaluating PI in OPSD training.

papers.title: Text-to-Image Generative Modeling Without Language Pretraining
papers.abstract: Modern text-to-image (T2I) systems use internet-scale language pretraining for text-conditioned image generation. We ask whether language pretraining is necessary for strong T2I generation. We introduce Halcyon, a family of early-fusion multimodal autoregressive models pretrained entirely from scratch on GPIC, a dataset of 100M image-text pairs. Halcyon-0.52B outperforms LlamaGen-XL/8 (48.0 vs. 63.3 gFD) with 18.2times less pretraining compute. Further, Halcyon-1.6B outperforms JiT-T2I-XXL/8++ (35.3 vs. 41.0 gFD) with 275times less pretraining compute. Controlled experiments show that text-only pretraining does not improve T2I generation. Halcyon also learns image captioning by replacing caption dropout with I2T supervision, maintaining competitive T2I generation quality under the same pretraining budget. We show that strong T2I systems can be trained from scratch without internet-scale language pretraining. Code and models are available at https://cs.stanford.edu/~keshik/halcyon

papers.title: RSIFlow: Adaptive Self-Improvement Workflows with an Evolving Meta-Agent
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in complex tasks, including code generation, tool use, and multi-hop question answering. Existing self-improvement methods enhance agent performance through model optimization, harness evolution, and executable artifact refinement, while recursive self-improvement (RSI) further extends optimization to the improvement mechanisms themselves. However, adapting self-improvement workflows to evolving performance bottlenecks while improving workflow orchestration through execution feedback remains a key challenge. We propose RSIFlow, a Recursive Self-Improvement framework that integrates adaptive workflow orchestration with meta-agent capability evolution. RSIFlow diagnoses performance bottlenecks from task-agent trajectories and environmental feedback to dynamically select component-specific improvement workflows. The meta-agent then distills workflow outcomes into component-specific skills and cross-component principles, evolving its own harness to improve subsequent workflow orchestration. Experiments across six benchmarks and two backbone models show that RSIFlow achieves the SOTA average performance on all benchmarks. Ablation studies further demonstrate the contributions of adaptive workflow orchestration and meta-harness evolution. Code is available at https://github.com/1HUAN1/RSI-Flow.

papers.title: Empowering Edge Agents: A Systematic Analysis of Edge-Cloud Collaboration in LLM Agent Execution
papers.abstract: Edge-cloud collaboration combines the lower inference overhead and greater data locality of edge-side execution with the stronger capabilities of cloud-hosted models. However, as LLM agents increasingly operate in long-horizon scenarios, cloud participation becomes interleaved throughout execution rather than a one-shot decision for each query. Such interleaved participation introduces trajectory-level effects that remain insufficiently understood. To address this gap, we introduce EC2-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating edge-cloud collaboration in long-horizon agent execution. It provides executable digital-workspace agent tasks and a unified evaluation framework covering task performance, resource usage, and privacy exposure. Using this benchmark, we empirically study diverse forms of edge-cloud collaboration. Our study reveals three findings. First, collaboration achieves a favorable balance among task performance, resource usage, and privacy exposure compared with edge-only and cloud-only execution. Second, as edge models become stronger, collaborative execution approaches cloud-only performance, and performance differences across strategies shrink, while privacy exposure remains strongly strategy-dependent. Third, stronger edge capability shifts preferred collaboration from externally controlled cloud participation and direct cloud execution toward more edge-controlled collaboration. Further analyses identify cloud-invocation decision-making and instruction following as important edge-side abilities for effective collaboration. These findings provide a systematic understanding of edge-cloud collaboration in long-horizon agent execution and insights for designing future edge agents that effectively collaborate with cloud models. Code and resources are available at https://github.com/OpenBMB/EC2-Bench.

papers.title: Heterogeneous Agentic Coevolution
papers.abstract: Recent advances in self-improving LLM agents have demonstrated the potential of AI systems that drive their own intelligence. However, many domain-specific applications rely on specialized foundation models that possess strong domain expertise but remain dependent on human-designed improvements. Extending recursive self-improvement to these models presents a key challenge: as a specialist improves, the strategies used to advance it must also adapt. To address this challenge, we propose Heterogeneous Agentic CoEvolution (HACE), a framework that jointly evolves specialized foundation models and LLM agents through reciprocal learning. HACE improves the specialist through supervised learning while training the agent with on-policy reinforced self-training, guided by verified performance gains on the current specialist. The agent's exploration, in turn, informs subsequent specialist training, enabling both models to adapt to each other's progress. To sustain this reciprocal learning, HACE further employs evolutionary search to optimize their interaction harness, adapting how the models exchange information and select training experiences as their capabilities evolve. We evaluate HACE across three challenging domains: recommendation systems, protein function prediction in biology, and crystal stability prediction in material discovery. We show that HACE outperforms the evaluated self-improving methods on the primary task metrics across all three domains. These results shed light on heterogeneous coevolution as a universal approach to improving specialized foundation models through reciprocal interaction with a learning agent.

papers.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
papers.abstract: One of the first steps of a research pipeline is generating ideas. Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate this step, but most of this work optimizes the quality of individual ideas, while overlooking diversity. In our work, we study document-grounded ideation, focusing on increasing the diversity of LLM generated ideas and ensuring they are high quality. Given prior papers, a model must propose a set of ideas that are each high-quality and clearly distinct from one another, while also being grounded in the input documents. To optimize for this, we propose training with a set-level reinforcement learning objective. In our setup, in a single generation, the model writes K structured idea cards grounded in the source papers, and the set is scored jointly, where each idea's quality is weighted by its distance from the ideas written before it. This teaches the model to steer each new idea away from its predecessors. We show that our trained 8B model achieves higher creative utility (a measure combining quality and diversity) than Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-6 Astra on our contamination-free benchmark. In a pilot human study with four experts, our sets are judged as promising as Claude Opus 4.8's and contain marginally more unique ideas. When a coding agent runs proof-of-concept experiments on the ideas, our model's success@k is comparable to Claude Opus 4.8's, so we see that the added diversity does not cost any executability.

papers.title: CyberArena: Benchmarking AI Agents in Live Symmetric Attack-and-Defense Combat
papers.abstract: AI agents are demonstrating increasingly strong offensive and defensive cybersecurity capabilities in the real world. Current benchmarks mostly evaluate agents in isolation against static targets. Real cyber operations, however, are dynamic and coupled: security postures constantly change as attackers and defenders adapt to each other in real time. Static benchmarks quickly saturate and miss an agent's ability to attack and defend simultaneously under live pressure. To address this gap, we present CyberArena, a dynamic, symmetric adversarial benchmark built around multi-round attack-and-defense combat. In isolated sandboxes, two agents compete under identical rules, acting concurrently as both attackers and defenders over continuously changing services. This converts static targets into evolving, semi-open challenges, directly testing an agent's speed and precision in discovering, exploiting, and patching vulnerabilities. To sustain the benchmark's longevity, an automated agentic pipeline continuously generates, reviews, and validates new environments. Furthermore, because pairwise contests are notoriously hard to quantify, we introduce a dynamical model that maps match dynamics into unified, multidimensional scores across offensive, defensive, and domain-specific capabilities. Evaluating 12 frontier LLM agents across 40 challenges in 466 matches, CyberArena separates model capabilities where single-agent baselines hit a ceiling. The trajectories read like a fight rather than an exam: defenders patch one hole and miss the next and certify repairs on stale evidence, while capable agents think a move ahead, planting backdoors for later rounds and, in one case, writing their own packet sniffer to watch the opponent. Beyond a benchmark, CyberArena serves as an adaptable, scalable experimental platform for future research on cybersecurity agents.

papers.title: ActionRoPE: action as coordinates for spatially consistent control in planar-camera game world models
papers.abstract: Game world models have made rapid progress toward real-time interactive generation. Yet action control is still predominantly implemented as feature conditioning, leaving the model to learn from training data how each action should move the visual world. This formulation is poorly matched to a broad class of planar-camera worlds, such as top-down and isometric games. In these worlds, player motion induces a geometrically well-defined planar camera displacement. We observe that the key to spatially consistent control in such worlds is to represent the effect of each action directly in world coordinates. To this end, we introduce ActionRoPE, a parameter-free action interface that converts action-driven camera displacement into world-coordinate rotary positions. As a result, tokens corresponding to the same world location retain the same positional address across time. These world coordinates further expose a spatial asymmetry in generation: regions covered by the initial observation are geometrically known, while newly revealed regions remain to be synthesized. We therefore propose Coordinate-Conditioned Noise Scheduling (CNS), which assigns token-wise denoising schedules according to this known-new structure. It allows observed regions to stabilize earlier, while new content is generated with reference to them. Compared with four representative action-conditioning mechanisms, our approach follows the commanded motion more faithfully and reduces the revisit drift by 66% over the strongest baseline. The same interface transfers across video backbones from 1.3B to 33B parameters and to out-of-distribution scenes. Project Page: https://teawhite.cn/ActionRoPE/

papers.title: Sparse Feature Policy Unlearning Mitigates State Hallucination in Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong generalization in robotic manipulation by leveraging rich representations from pretrained vision-language models. However, their deployment in real-world environments remains limited by recurring unreliable behaviors. In this work, we study state hallucination, a recurring failure pattern in which a VLA continues acting as if an unrealized robot-object state had been achieved. Our analyses find that state hallucination coincides with weakened attention to task-relevant visual regions, and a mechanistic interpretation via sparse autoencoders reveals that hallucination-associated sparse features are activated when these failures occur. Based on this analysis, we propose SOUL (Sparse feature pOlicy UnLearning), which selectively unlearns policy knowledge associated with state hallucination behaviors, where sparse features identified from hallucination failures and successful behaviors serve as explicit forgetting and retention targets, respectively. Experiments across VLA architectures in simulated and real-world environments show that our method substantially reduces hallucinated failures and improves task success without substantially compromising the existing manipulation capabilities. These results suggest that interpretable feature analysis provides a practical basis for selectively modifying undesirable knowledge in robot policies.

papers.title: HERA: Harness-Environment Co-Evolution for Reliable Agentic Abstention
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of acting in complex tool-use environments, yet they often fail to recognize when tasks are infeasible and no valid solution exists. Recent work has formalized this reliability gap as the problem of agentic abstention, and existing approaches typically optimize a model or agent harness against a fixed set of tasks, leading to limited generalization to unseen failure modes. We introduce HERA, a framework for harness-environment co-evolution for agentic abstention. HERA consists of (i) a pipeline to automatically construct verifiable pairs of feasible and infeasible tasks by applying controlled environment mutations that transform solvable tasks into cases requiring abstention, and (ii) a co-evolution procedure in which performance failures on previous tasks are used to drive harness adaptation and generate new execution environments and tasks geared towards previous weaknesses. On held-out evaluation tasks, an evolved harness from HERA improves abstention accuracy from 61.7% to 83.3% while improving feasible-task completion from 68.3% to 76.7%, achieving the highest abstention and feasible-task completion among the compared methods. The resulting best harness transfers across 19 other LLMs, improving abstention accuracy by 15.3 percentage points on average without any model-specific optimization, and enabling smaller models to match the performance of more powerful models at an estimated 85% lower cost.

papers.title: Token-Set Choice Confounds POPE: A Systematic Audit of Yes/No Extraction in VLM Hallucination Evaluation
papers.abstract: We set out to reproduce a recent hallucination-mitigation result on the POPE benchmark. The LLaVA-1.5-7B baseline we measured, 82.21 F1 on the adversarial split, sat 1.21 to 8.67 points above the adversarial baselines we planned to compare against (81.00, 79.30, and 73.54). We looked at the evaluation code and found a readout choice that moves F1 on its own. A two-token logit readout decides yes versus no by comparing two vocabulary IDs, 3582 ("yes") and 1217 ("no"). Across 9,000 greedy-decode questions spanning all three splits, neither ID is generated even once. The model emits " Yes" (token 3869) and " No" (token 1939), because SentencePiece prepends a space byte after the prompt suffix "ASSISTANT:". Read with an eight-token lookup that covers the space-prefixed surface forms, LLaVA-1.5-7B scores F1 0.8221, 0.8498, and 0.8713 on the adversarial, popular, and random splits. That 6.13-point adversarial shift exceeds the adversarial gain reported by five of the six papers we surveyed. None of them states its readout, and our reference ran under 4-bit NF4 quantization, so we cannot say how much of any reported gain a matched evaluation would keep. That comparison stays unresolved until readout and precision are matched. On the fixed baseline we run nine inference-time corrections of our own (none beat it) and dissect why the adversarial split resists logit-level intervention. In a 3,000-question probe, wrong predictions draw more image attention than correct ones (Cohen's d=-0.46, p=1.4times10^{-24}), the opposite of what grounding-based corrections assume. A four-readout audit across four further VLMs from three tokenizer families confirms the confound is protocol-level, not model-specific: porting the LLaVA-1.5 IDs verbatim drops F1 to 0.00 on the two disjoint-vocabulary models, whereas a tokenizer-derived readout holds between 0.80 and 0.92.

papers.title: Vision-Language-Delta-Action: Learning Compact Deltas as Actionable Transition Interfaces for Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation is not merely observation-to-action generation, but the realization of task-specified state changes in the physical world. Existing vision-language-action (VLA) methods directly learn observation-to-action mappings, imposing a substantial learning burden due to the gap between semantic understanding and action execution. Although world-action models (WAMs) improve control through future prediction, modeling complete future states wastes capacity on static appearance and action-irrelevant changes. We propose Vision-Language-Delta-Action (VLDA), a paradigm that reformulates full future prediction as compact actionable transition modeling. Its core is a compact Delta variable that captures latent world-state changes, serving as an interface between vision-language understanding and action generation. VLDA learns Delta through a unified objective composed of the Local Transition Filter (LT-Filter) and Global Transition Anchor (GT-Anchor). LT-Filter captures task-relevant manipulation-centric changes while suppressing static reconstruction biases. GT-Anchor provides coarse future-level regularization to preserve the overall direction of state changes. Delta-Driven Action Refinement (DDAR) further grounds Delta in the action manifold and injects it as a structured seed to guide action denoising. We implement VLDA within LoongForge, an open-source training framework for large-scale foundation and embodied models, using its modular and distributed infrastructure for unified two-stage optimization. Experiments show that VLDA improves long-horizon consistency, robustness, and generalization, validating actionable Delta as an alternative to direct action prediction and full future-state modeling.

papers.title: QD-Rec: Open-Ended Evolution of Recommendations via Quality-Diversity
papers.abstract: Open-ended search combined with foundation models has produced advances such as faster algorithms, new results on open mathematical problems, and self-improving agents. We extend this paradigm to recommendation for decision-making, focusing on decisions where the set of possible choices is fixed but the reasons for choosing them are not. In high-stakes decisions, e.g., which company to acquire or which customer to target, comparing diverse, well-reasoned options can be more useful than a single ranked list. We formalize open-ended recommendation as building a diverse, high-quality set of recommendations, each an item together with a hypothesis, a natural-language reason why the item fits the needs of a decision maker. We propose QD-Rec, a quality--diversity method that selects items with a contextual bandit and generates hypotheses with a foundation model from earlier ones kept in an archive as stepping stones. A new recommendation enters the archive if it is novel or better than its nearest neighbor. Across M&A, customer targeting, and paper and book recommendation, QD-Rec gives the highest mean quality and builds the largest archive in most settings.

papers.title: A Language-Informed Loss for Visual Generation
papers.abstract: End-to-end visual generation with pixel-space loss has recently achieved competitive performance without the need for learned image tokenizers. In this work, we study whether language-informed supervision can provide a richer training signal than pixel loss for visual generation. We introduce LILIE (pronounced "lily"), a Language-Informed and Lossless Image Encoder. LILIE is an invertible image transform trained such that a vision-language model can recover captions from noised features. The encoder uses a normalizing flow transformer trained jointly with a vision-language model via next token prediction. We then use the encoder to extract a simple language-informed loss for text-to-image generation. We train JiT models with LILIE loss, reducing gFD by 14 points (66.84 to 53.01) against a pixel-only baseline on the GPIC dataset. Our code, encoders, and generative models are available at https://suchiragarwal.com/lilie.

papers.title: Measuring Mechanistic Uncertainty in Large Language Models via Causal Robustness
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in critical domains, where their susceptibility to hallucinations makes reliable and interpretable uncertainty quantification essential. We introduce the concept of mechanistic uncertainty, which characterizes uncertainty through the stability of the internal mechanisms supporting a model's response. We propose the causal robustness margin, defined as the minimum internal intervention required to deviate the model's output, and operationalize it using Jacobian Lens (Jlens) concept steering vectors. Across three open-source models and five question-answering datasets, we show incorrect and uncertain responses exhibit smaller margins, indicating greater sensitivity to internal interventions, and the causal robustness margin complements conventional output-based uncertainty methods. Finally, in a controlled knowledge injection experiment, correctly learned facts show increased margins after training, suggesting that causal robustness provides a mechanistically grounded signal of uncertainty.

papers.title: Any 3D Scene is Worth 1K Tokens: 3D-Grounded Representation for Scene Generation at Scale
papers.abstract: Scene-level 3D generation has long been dominated by 2D multi-view or video diffusion models. Typically, these 2D-based approaches perform scene generation in a 2D latent space, which introduces two fundamental issues: (i) representing 3D scenes via 2D views leads to significant representation redundancy, and (ii) latent space rooted in 2D inherently limits the spatial consistency of the generated scenes. In this paper, we propose to perform 3D scene generation directly within a high-dimensional implicit 3D latent space derived from powerful 2D foundation models (e.g., DINOv2, SigLIP2, DA3). Then we tame diffusion transformers to perform diffusion modeling directly in the 3D latent space, enabling 3D-grounded scene generation. In our experiments, we not only demonstrate the advantages of our method over 2D-based approaches in terms of efficiency and spatial consistency, but also comprehensively analyze the impact of 3D latent representation on 3D scene generation performance. Furthermore, we validate the favorable scalability of our method with respect to representation and model capacity.

papers.title: Beyond Maliciousness: Static and Runtime Attack-Surface Profiling of Agent Skills
papers.abstract: Agent skills are Markdown documents that a tool-using agent reads as instructions and then acts on with the privileges of the session that loaded them. Installing one grants authority (the standing to direct the agent, not new privilege), and the size of that grant is what we measure. We present a two-phase attack-surface profiling methodology that combines whole-bundle static analysis and dependency provenance checking with instrumented sandbox execution and separate model-based assessment of the resulting traces. We apply the methodology to 6,309 listings from two marketplaces, selecting listings for execution without conditioning that decision on a prior threat or risk signal. Half the corpus carries evidence of shell-execution capability; the corresponding shares are 35% for filesystem read, 31% each for filesystem write and network egress, and 13% for credential access; seven listings in ten carry at least one elevated capability. That is the surface a user accepts at install time, and almost none of it is visible then. A permission model exists but is close to inert. Authors may list the tools a skill pre-approves in its own frontmatter, which removes confirmation prompts rather than restricting what the skill can reach; of the 6,061 listings whose frontmatter parses, 770 declare anything at all, the vocabulary cannot express credential or environment access, and nothing checks what it does express against the bundle. Declaring is also not declaring accurately: 59% of declaring listings understate what their bundle can do. ClawHub declares roughly twice as often as skillsmp, yet under-declares on 88% of its declarations against 31%. Triage at the marketplace boundary therefore cannot rest on what a listing declares. It must rest on what the bundle can do. These results position capability-oriented attack-surface profiling as a necessary complement to maliciousness detection.

papers.title: SPARC: Spoken Profile Authorship Recognition Corpus
papers.abstract: Speech anonymization has focused on the acoustic signal, leaving open how much speaker information the transcribed words themselves retain. In this work, we study pairwise speaker and demographic-attribute verification from transcribed speech. We introduce SPARC (Spoken Profile Authorship Recognition Corpus), a benchmark built from two podcast corpora comprising over 12,500 speakers, 1.5M quality-filtered utterances, and speaker-level inferred or source-provided labels for sex, age, and accent, and evaluate five attribution models and three LLMs on identity- and attribute-verification trials with episode- and metadata-based topic proxies. LLM adversaries distinguish same-speaker pairs from text alone. Attribute-label agreement is harder to verify, but LLMs perform sex- and accent-label verification above chance. Finally, releasing only short probe texts (50 words) degrades the strongest adversaries the most, offering a partial reduction in observed linkage.

papers.title: TokenGate: Adapting LLMs for Fast and Memory-Efficient Prefill with Learned Token Pruning
papers.abstract: Expert human readers process large inputs (e.g., code repositories and long documents) by skimming to closely read only what matters. On the other hand, language models process all input tokens through each model layer, resulting in significant processing costs for long-context inputs. We introduce TokenGate, a small, drop-in component that extends existing trained models to enable end-to-end learnable token pruning over long-context inputs for fast and memory-efficient prefill. To enable end-to-end learning despite the non-differentiable top-K operator for token pruning, we introduce token-gated attention, a mechanism inspired by Mixture-of-Experts that re-weights attention logits using token importance scores. Across diverse tasks, TokenGate achieves 1.4-11.3times faster time-to-first token (TTFT) and 1.5-3.4times lower peak memory at no accuracy degradation for prefill in transformers. Compared to the best-performing prior methods for token-pruning, TokenGate gives up to 6.4times faster prefill and 2times lower peak memory. TokenGate natively extends both standard transformers (e.g., Qwen3) and hybrid-attention models (e.g., Qwen3.5) with simple lightweight adaptation comparable to standard parameter-efficient fine-tuning. We make our code available at: https://github.com/tokengate-models/TokenGate.

papers.title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
papers.abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.

papers.title: Legal Guidance in the Wild: How Users Seek Legal Help in Real-World LLM Conversations
papers.abstract: People ask conversational AI models about their legal rights, obligations, procedures, and personal situations that may have legal consequences. To study this behavior, we first need to distinguish requests for legal guidance from other legally themed discussions and unrelated conversations. We contribute a multi-axis taxonomy of legal queries capturing whether legal guidance is sought, how a request is formulated, and which legal domains it concerns; apply it to 2,122 naturally occurring WildChat-1M conversations; and create a human-reviewed gold evaluation set of 200 conversations. All annotations, model checkpoints, and evaluation code are publicly available. In this enriched sample, 71.1% of conversations containing legal content seek personalized or practical guidance. Rights-and-options advice is the most common primary request type among legal-content conversations, and 25.3% of guidance-positive conversations span multiple legal topics. The gold evaluation set supports a two-stage comparison of ModernBERT-base and ModernBERT-large against a TF-IDF cascade. Our framework supports large-scale studies of legal guidance in conversational AI, and the public release of the annotated data facilitates reproducible research and future model development.

papers.title: RealityBench: Simulated Environments to Evaluate a Vision Language Model's Ability to Document Human Physical Work
papers.abstract: Augmenting worker capabilities in the physical world through guidance has been a decades-long goal for AI agents. One key supporting capability is to understand what the worker is doing, seeing through the human's camera or smart glasses, and assist them in documentation. Despite advances in vision language models, their capabilities in these settings remain uncertain and are challenging to benchmark because most physical work data is proprietary, and involves too much variability to study in a principled manner. Unlike structured settings such as kitchens and warehouses that have predictable lighting, geometry, and objects, field-facing tasks such as rooftop solar installation and vehicle repair are unconstrained and high variance. Here, we model real-world physical work in Blender across eleven environments, incorporating variants in both image acceptability and documentation. The acceptability task asks whether a particular view would be suitable proof-of-work and documentation asks whether an agent can understand the task-relevant state of the environment from that view. Across 26 vision-language models, we find that top models largely solve documentation when the answer is text in frame, but are weak at reading measurements and at judging small parts and spatial relations, such as whether a tape measure leans. Acceptability is harder to pin down because human raters disagree with each other. Measured against a scorer that agrees with the raters' majority about as often as a single rater does, the best models cannot be distinguished from a single non-author rater, at a cost within the range of a human pass. In the three environments where we can trace acceptability errors, most wrong rejections come from misreading the scene rather than the requirement. On the three documentation questions for which we have real images, model rankings on rendered frames transfer to real images.

papers.title: Vision as Proprioception: Estimating Humanoid Robot Pose from Video
papers.abstract: Estimating a humanoid robot's internal state from video has a wide range of real-world applications but remains unexplored. During interactions with a robot, its onboard state information may be unavailable due to privacy, ownership, or communication constraints. Meanwhile, online and AI-generated robot videos provide rich sources of data but typically lack corresponding joint configurations, limiting their direct use in robot learning. To address these issues, we present HumanoidPose, a new framework that treats vision as proprioception to recover full-body joint configurations in world space from video alone. Specifically, we combine pretrained human-pose features with robot kinematics in a unified model that predicts each embodiment's joint configurations. We retarget human motions to sixteen different humanoid embodiments, enabling scalable learning entirely from synthetic data. To improve real-world generalization, we further leverage unlabeled online videos through self-training to develop a 2D robot-pose detector. In our evaluation, HumanoidPose improves joint-angle and joint-position accuracy over the evaluated baselines and reduces joint-angle error by 18-32% relative to the best-performing baseline on each of the three real humanoid platforms. We further show improved global localization and generalization to unseen embodiments. HumanoidPose enables visual understanding of other robots during interaction and extraction of robot motion from online and generated videos.

papers.title: First Passage Attention
papers.abstract: Augmenting softmax attention with forget gates typically relies on summing decay contributions along the key--query path. Because such accumulation is monotonic, these mechanisms cannot selectively erase intermediate context while preserving older, structurally relevant tokens. We propose First Passage Attention (FPA), which shifts from path summation to path extrema by lowering a key's logit proportionally to the deepest dip of a learned scalar field below that key's level over the intervening span. FPA encompasses the Forgetting Transformer (FoX) as a special case, and when the field and levels follow a shared learned walk, the alive keys with unpenalised logits naturally form a stack. We show that a constant-dimension FPA head realises any subset of keys left alive by subsequent dips, whereas softmax heads with positional biases or token-level forget gates require a head dimension linear in the number of keys. In synthetic experiments, one-layer FPA heads converge to these target sets while comparable softmax and FoX baselines fail on every seed. Scaling to a 110M-parameter language model, FPA matches FoX in perplexity and uniquely achieves perfect passkey retrieval at 8times the training length, even with its key--value cache compressed to about 25%.

papers.title: Competence-Based Evaluation of Logical Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have brought impressive performance across diverse tasks; however, shortcomings remain in logical reasoning, including inconsistencies under linguistic variation. To improve the reasoning capacity of LLMs, we must be able to accurately measure their reasoning capacity. Current benchmarks primarily report single accuracy numbers on selected reasoning tasks. Such a performance-based evaluation methodology says little about a model's generalization capacity in reasoning. To address this limitation, we argue for a different evaluation paradigm, called competence-based evaluation (CBE), which tests whether models reliably apply the same competence across a family of problems. A parameterized generator scales complexity while keeping the required competence fixed, and matched answer-preserving presentations test correctness beyond one formulation. We instantiate CBE on elementary ordering tasks, scaling input size while varying presentations of the same ordering rule. Across six GPT and Qwen models, performance is reasonably good over bounded complexity ranges, but even strong models fail the competence condition across the tested family. Chain-of-thought and GRPO extend strong performance without resolving all tested failures; supervised LoRA shows little held-out transfer. CBE provides diagnostic profiles and an evaluation protocol that can grow with future models.
